summary:
Sky is an agentic clinical assistant supporting astronauts and flight surgeons. Our solution helps astronauts monitor, understand, and respond to health issues in space. The main capabilities include proactive prevention (baseline tracking, identifying abnormalities, and anticipating risks) and emergency support (real-time guidance following NASA medical protocols and flight surgeon sync). 

Sky helps the flight surgeon stay informed through health updates, risk warnings, and synchronized medical information. It leads to faster and better-informed decisions, making space exploration safer for everyone.
details:
How it works: Sky interacts with astronauts and flight surgeon(s) via text or voice. Its responses are based on the astronauts' data and NASA standard protocols. Through Sky, astronauts can view their vital metrics at a glance. The body hologram feature helps astronauts better visualize these health metrics and better describe their symptoms.

Data pipeline: We used ChatGPT and Claude to support background research and to help identify and search for datasets provided by NASA, including the NASA Life Sciences Portal (NLSP), NASA OSDR,... . These tools were used only for information gathering and search assistance. All information and data sources suggested by the tools were checked against the original NASA records and published literature. The authors take full responsibility for the accuracy and integrity of this work.

Development process:
Sky was developed using a spec-first, AI-assisted development workflow with human supervision.

We began by researching NASA medical standards, astronaut health challenges, and publicly available space-health datasets. Based on this research, we defined the system architecture, product requirements, and UI/UX specifications.

The application was then built using multiple AI coding agents powered by OpenCode, coordinated through the herd-core CLI. Each agent worked on an independent feature branch, while a human reviewer supervised integration. All changes went through code review, type checking, and testing before merging.

We followed an iterative development process, continuously implementing, testing, and deploying features such as real-time health monitoring, AI clinical assistance, voice interaction, and 3D astronaut health visualization.

The application was deployed on AWS EC2 using automated Nix-based deployment pipelines.


AI Development: OpenCode, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock, PI SDK, hc CLI.

Frontend: TypeScript, React 19, TanStack Start, Tailwind CSS v4, Three.js, React Three Fiber, shadcn/ui, OpenUI.

Backend: Bun, TypeScript, Drizzle ORM, SQLite, Zod, REST APIs, WebSockets.

AI & Voice: PI SDK (multi-agent architecture), ElevenLabs Speech Engine, ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech.

Design & Multimedia: Google Stitch, Three.js, HyperFrames.

Data & Research: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), NASA-STD-3001, public astronaut health research datasets.

Development & Deployment: Git, GitHub, Bun, Turborepo, Nix Flakes, AWS EC2, Caddy, systemd, Git LFS.

Testing: Vitest, Bun Test, TypeScript type checking.

Other uses of AI tools: Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT were used for topic research, information gathering and consolidation, video presentation.
